newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber higher on Palembang deal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber higher on Palembang deal.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices were higher in early trading on Tuesday after deals in Palembang, traders said.
They said a deal was done overnight at 47.75 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for August shipment, which prompted offer prices in other centres to rise.

"Prices show eda tendency to rise this morning after the deal in Palembang. There was a possibility that Chinese buyers have entered the market, but they usually do purchasing quietly so it's hard to find the exact details," said one trader in Jakarta.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 48.00 fob Medan, at 47.75-48.00 fob Surabaya, at 47.50 fob Padang and at 46.75 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
Chinese buyers were reportedly looking to buy Indonesian rubber following the Thai government's intervention in the domestic market to prop up prices.
Indonesian traders said activities had returned to normal in rubber factories in Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan after a riot last week in which 142 people were reported to have died in a fire.
"Basically, the riot did not affect the production because the factories are located outside Banjarmasin," said another trader.
